rv.q: Michael Grandage's powerful, captivating production offers an informative and haunting portrayal of Dr Rosalind Franklin
It is a commanding, intelligent performance and my only complaint about Anna Ziegler's intriguing, informative 95-minute play is that it is not longer.

Michael Grandage's superb 95-minute production expertly balances its energies as detective thriller and as interactive speculation about the hovering moments where her life could have taken a different turning.
It is a tribute to Kidman and to Michael Grandage's fleet direction that despite all this, Photograph 51 transmits excitement and a real sense of discovery.
This show clicks like the shutter of a hi-tech laboratory camera.
However, the final quarter-hour or so of the 90-minute piece becomes increasingly glib and self-serving.
It tells an exciting story, but there is a chilliness at its heart, and Kidman's Franklin is the chilliest of the lot.
Her eerily symmetrical face is absorbing to look at but for a limited time.
The play lacks drama but it's a good story, with Kidman, like Franklin finally, the undisputed star.
